name: whitman-three-editions
description: Real public-domain N-WITNESS edition case (BACKLOG B4, ≥3 witnesses, exercising the variant graph on real text): the SHARED opening three stanzas of Walt Whitman's 'Song of Myself' across THREE editions of Leaves of Grass — 1855, 1860, and 1891-92. This is the authentic 'one author, many editions' shape the variant graph was designed for. The text genuinely evolves: 1855 'I celebrate myself,' → (1860 same line) → 1891 'I celebrate myself, and sing myself,'; the 1860 edition adds section numbers (1. 2. 3.) and capitalises 'Soul'; the four-dot 1855 ellipses become an em-dash in 1860 and a comma in 1891. NOTE the passage is restricted to the three stanzas common to all three editions (the 1891 'My tongue…/Creeds…' insertions, collated separately in case 18, are omitted here so the graph compares like-for-like). The 1855 and 1860 witnesses are OCR (Internet Archive) hand-corrected against canonical transcriptions, retaining authentic edition features; 1891 is verbatim (Gutenberg #1322). Base = 1855. See docs/development/CASE_STUDY.md.
